mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a weakening economy, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a 3-month decline in GDPC1, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals labor market weakness, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE increases by > 0.5%, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in one month signals supply-side weakness, leading to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO drops by > 1%, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and decrease in housing starts (HOUST) indicates inflationary pressures without corresponding demand, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases and HOUST decreases, or if the joint effect of these variables on 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, leading to increased wage pressures and reduced corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, or if the joint effect of these variables on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 3% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased liquidity and investment in equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 3%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a strengthening economy, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a 3-month increase in GDPC1, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
